convoLines.text: "Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "June owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Sleep's gone strange. I braid grass while listening to plans at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Diego grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Diego is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"The water goes glass-still. That's The Living Wire telling you it's about to move. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"This one — Chinese Chive. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"I don't answer that one myself. Not yet. Maybe when I've decided whether surviving counts as an excuse or just a reason. You'd know about that."
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"I dreamed June was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"June always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
Everything else is luxury. Breathing tomorrow is the whole game.
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Survival isn't pretty. It's Tuesday. It's boring and relentless and I choose it."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on wanting to survive, whatever it takes."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "June is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Diego is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"No sound. That's Night Court telling you it's about to move. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"This one — Cow Parsley. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Since June died... I keep expecting to see June at the fire. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Diego nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I clean up other people's messes quietly for June, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"You saw it too, right? Who Ate It?. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
I'll do what it takes. I'll live with what I've done. That's the deal.
"I've made peace with doing what I have to. The peace is uneasy, but it's peace."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Like I said — Still on wanting to survive, whatever it takes."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Farid and Sam — Who Ate It?, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Take your time."
"What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Mateo nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d12: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. June Jain is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d12: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d12: 🕯️ June Jain is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d12: What June kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d12: "June's gone." Diego looks at you for a long moment. "You're not June." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d12: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Jorge blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d12: 📖 LEARNED: Shoulder Check (Level 1). You know exactly where to hit something with your shoulder so it goes where YOU want. Shove a controlled monster 2 tiles — into its friends, away from yours.

d12: 📖 LEARNED: Hogtie (Level 1). Rope, a dazed monster, and thirty seconds of not being eaten. Hogtie a controlled monster: rooted 3 rounds (diminishing), and it can't wind up telegraphs. It can still lash out — the rope holds position, not malice.
d12: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d12: 📖 The Codex turns a page: June Jain, 12 days. The mantle passes to Jorge Silva.
d12: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Jorge Silva, 50 — a Rancher. His hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d12: The village's quarrel was with June — and June is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d12: At the grave, Diego, Mateo speak for Jorge — "June trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d12: The fire knew Jorge before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
